text_summary.body: Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer, sad at news of Jerusalem's broken wall, asks Artaxerxes in Nisan of his twentieth year to send him to build the city of his fathers' tombs; the king grants letters to the governors beyond the River and to the keeper of the king's forest for timber for the citadel gates, the city wall and a house.

setting.body: On Babylonian reckoning Artaxerxes I's twentieth year began 1 Nisan = 13 Apr 445. Anderson instead dates 1 Nisan 445 to 14 March from an astronomical new moon of 13 March.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V10B5R4WH4CZ9SZG2M71Y1
constraints.textual_assertion: In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king
assumptions: Nisan reckoning: year 20 began 1 Nisan = 13 Apr 445 (Parker & Dubberstein table).

Neh 1:1 places Chislev "in the twentieth year" before Nisan of the twentieth year, which suggests an autumn (Tishri) year count; on that count the Nisan in question is spring 444. Not modelled here; recorded as a competing reconstruction.

competing_reconstructions.label: Spring 444 BC (Tishri reckoning)
proponents: Autumn new-year solution, one of three listed by Noss & Thomas (UBS Handbook, 2005)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Neh 1:1 (Chislev, year 20) precedes 2:1 (Nisan, year 20); counting years from an autumn new year makes this consistent and puts the Nisan in 444.

competing_reconstructions.label: Emend Neh 1:1 to "the nineteenth year", or count from the accession day
competing_reconstructions.summary: Either a textual emendation or a count of regnal years from the king's accession anniversary rather than a calendar new year. Noss & Thomas advise translating the text as it stands.

open_questions: Horn & Wood (1954) on the Elephantine double dates and Judean regnal reckoning not accessible.

not_applicable.commentary: Enduring Word on Ezra/Nehemiah was not consulted in this Daniel session; Guzik's dates are recorded on the seventy-weeks prophecy.
